result.title: What Language Adds, and at What Cost: Four Controlled Probes of Pathology Vision-Language Models
result.summary: Vision--language models (VLMs) promise to make computational pathology queryable and able to draft reports, but how much language adds beyond the vision backbone is unclear, because almost every system is evaluated by its developers on test sets of their own choosing. We grade published evidence by how it was produced and test four claims with controlled probes that reuse released checkpoints and public data, varying one input at a time. Report text adds prognostic signal: adding a frozen embedding of the stage-redacted report to a slide embedding raises the pooled C-index by 0.019 for progression-free interval and by 0.016 for overall survival across 1{,}633 TCGA patients, and restoring the stage statement adds nothing. Prompts add no measurable accuracy at inference: with features and pooling fixed, zero-shot classification is statistically indistinguishable from a supervised linear probe for lung and renal cancer subtyping. Slide-level question answering is barely grounded: SlideChat answers 74.82\% of SlideBench-VQA(TCGA) items correctly with the slide and 74.41\% without it, whereas its language backbone alone reaches 43.52\%. Paraphrasing leaves accuracy unchanged but flips 8--23\% of answers. Self-reported gains from agentic navigation and few-shot language priors cannot yet be attributed to language. Language thus adds real but narrow value, and we propose minimum controls that would expose these failure modes in future evaluations.

AI.brief_summary: 论文对病理 VLM 做四项受控探针，复用已发布 checkpoint 与公开数据、每次只改一个输入，量化语言相对视觉骨干的增益，并揭示语言先验、提示与 agentic 导航收益难以归因的问题。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接触及 LVR 关心的视觉证据是否被真正使用：报告文本有信号、提示无增益、去掉切片仍答对 74.41%、改述翻转 8–23% 答案，可能为检验视觉 grounding、视觉旁路与贡献分配提供可控探针设计线索。
